payload_and_transport_work_verified_here: Shipped WebAssembly carries no DWARF: the 46 browser artifacts fall from 419 MiB to 69.7 MiB, and the largest artifact (5.7 MiB) is below the browser's 8 MiB synchronous compile limit. The Chromium fixture that maps a real wasm panic frame to Rust source through client_bg.wasm.map still passes.
Cold page load 20.9 MB and reload 1.2 MB; Host CPU per page load 2.06 s cold, then 0.15 s once the encoded body is replayed for a revision-addressed target.
Lossless JSON string conversion decodes and encodes runs instead of characters: to_utf16 1,925 ms to 46 ms and encode_utf16 below the sampling threshold on one cold session open.

A Definition's run of update Matches folds in one call: one decode, every Match applied against the state the previous one left, one encode. Measured per plugin module over one cold open of the same session, ui-conversation 1,545 ms to 1,380 ms, ui-trajectory 1,244 ms to 1,074 ms, client total 4,970 ms to 4,630 ms and the open 4,856 ms to 4,528 ms, two runs per side holding to about 0.2%. Verified afterwards by the same keyless run and navigation gate listed above.

A literal ASCII run decodes to UTF-16 one unit per byte instead of dispatching on each character's encoded width. `extend_desugared` under `JsonRef::to_utf16` falls from 266 ms to 62-76 ms per cold open, ui-conversation from 1,380 ms to 1,354 ms and ui-trajectory from 1,073 ms to 1,049 ms.

A history entry builds its wire envelope directly instead of serializing the durable event to JSON text and parsing it back. Measured on the real 6.9 MB history response by alternating the two builds: 264 ms to 243 ms, eight per cent, consistent across four warm iterations. An equivalence test asserts the direct envelope equals the round trip in value and in serialized text for escapes, large and fractional numbers, absent and empty optionals, both surface-operation variants and a negative timestamp; history, subagent-history and schema parity suites pass, as do web-navigation and the full keyless suite.

A history page borrows the loaded window instead of deep-copying every event before selecting a suffix of it, and a tool result's backscan reads through an iterator so the live event stream keeps passing its session's own list. Measured on the real 6.9 MB history response by alternating the two builds over eight iterations: 239.4 ms to 236.9 ms with no overlap, and the transient copy of the whole window per request is gone.
remaining: The client's remaining per-event cost is the wasm boundary itself: the frames carrying no script URL (TextDecoder.decode and encodeInto over the 8 MB body) 431 ms and client-runtime 592-614 ms are now the two largest modules of a 2.6 s open. The source keeps session data as JavaScript values and converts nothing, so closing this means changing what crosses the boundary per event rather than localizing a hot function.

A cold session open of an 8 MB history is 2.62 s against the source harness's 0.48 s on the same payload. The Host serves the history in 335 ms, so 2.2 s is the client folding 36,196 assistant/chunk events. Per module over one open: client-runtime 614 ms, no-url 431 ms, ui-conversation 301 ms, ui-trajectory 195 ms, idle about 335 ms, program about 171 ms.

Every remaining measured item is under 25 per cent of an open, so the next step has to be structural: the JSON text of each session event still crosses into every plugin's own wasm instance and is parsed there.
measurement_note: Wall clock at the 5-10% level is not measurable on this machine while another session compiles: the same committed source measured 4.29-4.62 s and later 4.63-5.04 s. Changes of this size are resolved by per-plugin-module profile self-time instead, where two runs of the same build hold to about 0.2%. The fold above was measured that way and then confirmed by the cold-open total, where the same policy holds.

differential_client_cost.method: The same visible session opened in the built port and in the pinned source harness, capturing each history payload and profiling the browser

per_event_us.method: Client-side settle time of one cold open divided by the events in the history document (port 2,527 ms over 36,592 events)

content_arrival.source_harness: 65,137 characters of conversation at 465 ms after the click
content_arrival.port: 609 characters at 1 s, then 9,598 characters at 2,232 ms
content_arrival.method: The same click on the same visible session, polling the rendered conversation every 50 ms (perceived.mjs)

differential_client_cost.conclusion: The two implementations ship comparable payloads and the port ships fewer events than the source. Both publish the window atomically, and the port shows its first content at 2,232 ms against the source's 465 ms. The gap is a per-event constant in the client, not a payload, pagination or publication-strategy difference.

trajectory_share.method: The same session opened in the built port with the trajectory plugin enabled and disabled through a launcher patch overlay that sets disabled on the ui-trajectory row
trajectory_share.chat_output: 9,598 characters with the plugin and 9,582 without; the 16-character difference is exactly the Chat and Trajectory tab labels it provides
trajectory_share.conclusion: Folding a chunk run removed the per-chunk re-encoding these numbers measured, so the trajectory Definitions now cost 195 ms of a 2,619 ms cold open instead of about 1.4 s of 4.5 s. Both UI plugins together are 496 ms, about 19 per cent, and the deferred-HMR trade recorded below is correspondingly smaller.
trajectory_share.why_the_obvious_fix_was_not_taken: Registering those Definitions lazily on first Trajectory use would route through rebuild_registry, which re-folds the entire stored window with every Definition, so the first Trajectory open would pay the whole open cost again. Capturing that saving needs an assembler capability that folds the stored window for one newly registered Definition, plus a background fold after the first paint. That is a product trade, not a localized fix.

gates_note: Every web gate this repository exposes has now been run against the current tree: 14 gates, all passing. No feature bug was found by exercising them.
idle_explained: The 393 ms idle bucket in a cold open is predominantly the history round trip: the Host's response latency is 335 ms and the client cannot fold the window before the whole document arrives. The slice yields are not the cost, because the defer is a browser timer and 18 slices at 2,048 events cost about 4 ms each.

parity_gate.result: 16 pending and 3 ported but unverified, so the final manifest gate does not pass
parity_gate.reasons: The pending set is environmental rather than behavioural: the pwsh terminal browser suite needs a pwsh executable that is not installed, hmr-live needs a published package and a dev watcher, and the remaining suites need a real provider key, an e2b sandbox, or a Windows or Linux host. The three ported-but-unverified rows are the Landlock build and packed-install scripts, which are Linux-only, and the OTel exporter, whose native SDK cannot represent lone UTF-16 surrogates.
parity_gate.note: The same 19 rows were pending when this work started. Nothing in the web surface this objective names is among them.

gate_flakiness: Two keyless scenarios failed under load during this work and pass in isolation and in an undisturbed full run: steering timed out on a 10 s poll, and live-interactions reported a mode label golden mismatch. Both are consequences of a client that renders about ten times slower than the source under contention. Neither reproduces on a quiet machine.
rejected_after_measurement: Replacing the lossless round trip that builds the RPC response value with serde_json::to_value: the response must cross as a serde_json::Value, whose type cannot hold the lone UTF-16 surrogates a session's data can contain, so the lossless text and its parse are the fidelity gate rather than waste.

Folding a Definition's run of update Matches (kept, and measured at 7 per cent of an open) was measured once before at no change on wall clock alone and reverted; per-module profile self-time is the instrument that resolves changes of this size.

assistant_fold_work_verified_here.what_changed: A Definition update wrote each accepted Match into the state's JSON: for a streamed block that re-encoded the whole accumulated text of that block - text, reasoning and Tool call arguments alike - and revalidated and rescanned it, once per chunk. The batch fold now keeps the block it is still growing in PendingBlocks (crates/client-runtime/src/pending_blocks.rs), appends each delta's exact UTF-16 code units, and publishes every pending block once per fold. A block replaced wholesale by block-start, block-end, assistant/message or llm/retry is dropped from the fold, and the visibility scan reads the pending blocks so a still-growing block decides first_visible_seq and hidden exactly as a published one would.
assistant_fold_work_verified_here.equivalence_evidence: crates/client-ui-conversation/tests/assistant_fold_parity.rs drives one window - a leading Tool call run whose state stays hidden, text, reasoning, a replaced Tool call block, block-start, block-end and a final message - through the real assembler twice, batched and unbatched, and asserts the published chat snapshot is identical. crates/client-ui-trajectory/tests/assistant_definition_parity.rs holds the same check for the trajectory Definition, and crates/client-runtime/src/pending_blocks.rs unit-tests the load, replace, append and visibility rules.
